facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old woman presented for evaluation of her worsening skin condition
The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs were sparse and less than 5 mm long
her scalp hairs were coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy: Showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)

her scalp hairs were coarse and brittle

Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

concepts.why: The patient's skin condition is characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, which is consistent with psoriasis, and the skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis.
The patient's sparse and short eyebrow hairs, as well as coarse and brittle scalp hairs, are consistent with alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes hair loss.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with seborrheic dermatitis, a common skin condition that causes scaly patches and red skin.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris, a rare skin condition that causes constant inflammation and scaling.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with lichen planus, a chronic inflammatory condition that affects the skin and mucous membranes.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, a chronic autoimmune condition that causes skin lesions.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with keratosis pilaris, a common skin condition that causes dry, rough patches on the skin.

The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with ichthyosis vulgaris, a common genetic disorder that causes dry, scaly skin.
It explains the trichography finding of nodal swelling with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end.

rationales.F02: The condition's progression to involve 90% of the body surface area suggests a severe skin condition, which is more typical of psoriasis or pityriasis rubra pilaris.
rationales.F03: The presence of widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale is highly suggestive of psoriasis.
rationales.F04: Sparse eyebrow hairs are a common feature of alopecia areata and monilethrix.
rationales.F05: Coarse and brittle scalp hairs are a common feature of monilethrix.
rationales.F06: The skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis is highly suggestive of psoriasis.
rationales.F07: The trichography results are highly suggestive of monilethrix, which is characterized by nodal swelling and invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end.
